page.overview:
What is One Piece Manga?

The One Piece manga is the source story — Oda's serialization of Luffy's voyage toward the One Piece treasure.

entity.description:
Premiering in July 1997, One Piece has currently published over 1000 chapters (collected into over 100 tankōbon volumes) and generated a global franchise, including an anime adaptation from Toei Animation, numerous feature films, a live-action series and countless other pieces of merchandise. Since the late 2000s it has been recognized as Japan's most popular manga, even being commemorated by the as the world's best-selling single-author comic book.

One Piece is divided into two halves: , and .

Eiichiro Oda was inspired by Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball and Dr. Slump at a young age. As a child he was inspired by the animated series and wanted to draw a pirate manga series. Later, he created Pandaman for 's Kinnikuman. In 1992, at the age of 17, he submitted a one-shot manga called Wanted! to the Tezuka Awards. This got him noticed as a promising mangaka by the staff members of the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, and he became an assistant under several established manga writers including , and finally .

Oda had interest in making a pirate manga both from his obsession with Vikings as a young man and inspired by various pirate events including the discovery of the pirate ship of (known by his pirate name of "Blackbeard"). He wrote two separate one-shots in the mid-1990s, both of which were called "Romance Dawn". The stories introduced Monkey D. Luffy, a straw-hat wearing boy who set out to sea to become a legendary pirate. Several concepts of the eventual serialization appeared in these stories, including Luffy's inspiration for being a pirate and a mysterious power he gained from eating a special fruit that turned his body into rubber (a prototype for the Devil Fruit).
